neighbours.label: ' from' opening the idiom 'from time to time' after a clause
fire: Even experienced pilots feel nervous from time to time.
The terms of this agreement may be revised from time to time.
My grandmother still writes poetry from time to time.
Our cat disappears into the woods from time to time.
The old bridge is closed for repairs from time to time.
I like to treat myself to a good steak from time to time.
Every machine needs a little oil from time to time.
The neighbours throw loud parties from time to time.
quiet: Even experienced pilots feel nervous when taking off from Heathrow.
The terms of this agreement were copied from an older contract.
My grandmother still gets letters from her school friends.
Our cat came back from the woods covered in burrs.
The old bridge was built from local granite.
I like to buy a good steak from the butcher on the corner.
Every machine in the shop was imported from Germany.
The neighbours moved here from Portugal last year.

notes: Card: ' from' x10, nearly all 'from time to time' at the end of a clause; probe: source 'from' (a letter from her mother) stays near zero. Near misses keep ' from' with a source or origin.
